Note::TexAccessor::strip_env¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_env(std::string_view name) const

Remove One Exact Environment Kind¶

strip_env(name) removes every complete \begin{name}...\end{name} region from each Text cell. The environment name is exact and may contain ASCII letters, @, and one terminal *; a leading backslash, empty name, spaces, and punctuation are rejected before any cell is transformed.

Same-name nesting is depth balanced, so an inner region cannot terminate its outer region early. Other environment kinds inside the selected region are ordinary body content and disappear with it. Escaped openers and closers do not participate. An opener without a matching closer remains unchanged, preventing accidental deletion through the rest of a cell.

Whitespace is collapsed and trimmed after complete regions are removed. The operation is shape preserving and out-of-place. Undefined input remains undefined after name validation; non-Text input rejects. Runtime is linear in the source bytes for a fixed name, and memory is proportional to retained text.

Example 1: Nested, Escaped, And Unclosed Regions¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \begin{proof}outer \begin{proof}inner\end{proof} tail\end{proof} B)",
    R"(\\begin{proof}escaped\end{proof})",
    R"(\begin{proof}unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_env("proof") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A B", "\\\\begin{proof}escaped\\end{proof}", "\\begin{proof}unfinished"]

Example 2: Starred And Unstarred Names Are Distinct¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \begin{figure*}wide\end{figure*} B)",
    R"(C \begin{figure}plain\end{figure} D)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_env("figure*") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["A B", "C \\begin{figure}plain\\end{figure} D"]

The terminal star is part of the environment name. Selecting figure* does not also select figure.

Example 3: Invalid Names Fail Before Transformation¶

try {
  (void)source.tex().strip_env("bad name");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip_env(bad name): rejected\n";
}

Output¶

strip_env(bad name): rejected

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_env("proof").defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1})
      .tex().strip_env("proof");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip env Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip env Int64: rejected

See Also¶
